evidence: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 throws plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`; tRPC maps non-TRPCError throws to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). Sibling handler setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts:7,77 imports and throws TRPCError with explicit codes, so the convention in this router is TRPCError (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN).

packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-188 adds getCacheStatusByCredentialIds (groupBy + _max.updatedAt). A test file already exists for this repository (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.test.ts), but the diff adds no test for the new method. Coverage gap is real, but the method is a thin Prisma groupBy wrapper with low risk, so adding a test is optional.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1023-1024 calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) intending to bump updatedAt. SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is `DateTime? @updatedAt` (schema.prisma ~line 860). Prisma's query engine only injects @updatedAt values when the write args are non-empty; an empty data object is a no-op, so updatedAt is never touched. Should pass { updatedAt: new Date() } explicitly.

packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:1-6 keeps the Prisma-generated warning 'Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value', but line 9 does `ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" ... NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` and schema.prisma:1719 has @default(now()). The header is stale and misleading; harmless at runtime, so removing it is a low-priority cleanup.

CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:68-69: canDisconnect respects disableConnectionModification but hasCache does not, so cache delete still appears when EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375 passes disableConnectionModification={true}. The observation is accurate, but the flag's name and its previous use (it gated only DisconnectIntegration in the wrapper) suggest it is about connect/disconnect, and deleting the cache does not modify the credential. Whether to hide it is a product decision, not a bug.

CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:89 uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` while the surrounding string is translated via useLocale() (line 37). Non-English users get a US-formatted date (M/D/YY, 12h) inside a localized sentence. useLocale exposes i18n.language, which can be passed instead.

connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29 does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly. Elsewhere, packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-29 (CalendarCache.init) checks the global 'calendar-cache' feature flag and returns CalendarCacheRepositoryMock (whose new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns []) when the flag is off. So the handler runs an extra groupBy on every connectedCalendars call, and shows stale cache timestamps and a delete action even when the feature is disabled. Impact is modest because stale rows would usually be empty, but going through the flag-aware path is the established pattern.

calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27 declares getCacheStatusByCredentialIds() with no parameters. TypeScript allows fewer parameters when implementing an interface method, and the sibling mock methods (e.g. deleteManyByCredential() at line 23) also leave out unused params. It compiles and matches the file's convention; adding the parameter would only help readability.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 sets ENV_FILE="../.env", which resolves against $PWD. It only reaches the repo .env when run from scripts/. If run from the repo root it writes to the parent directory's .env, and lines 65-68 silently create that file if missing. This is a dev-only helper, so the fix ($(dirname "$0")/../.env) is low priority.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:72 uses `sed -i '' -E ...`. GNU sed treats '' as the script argument and fails ('can't read ... No such file' / unknown command), so on Linux the update fails when GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists. The script is a dev helper apparently written for macOS, so cross-platform support is a nice-to-have (e.g. write to a temp file and mv, or `sed -i.bak`).

apps/web/package.json:11 changes dev:cron to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. grep shows ts-node is a declared devDependency (apps/web/package.json:196) but tsx is not declared in root or apps/web package.json, so npx will download it on demand (needs network, unpinned version). This only affects a local dev script; adding tsx as a devDependency would fix it.

selectedCalendar.ts:400 types `data` as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput but forwards it to prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany (lines 401-404), whose data type is SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput | UncheckedUpdateManyInput. UpdateInput allows nested relation writes (user/credential/eventType) that updateMany rejects at runtime. Structural typing probably lets the current code compile, and the only caller passes {}, so this is a type-precision fix rather than a live bug.

CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-50: deleteCacheMutation has no onSettled invalidation, unlike disconnectMutation (lines 61-64), which invalidates connectedCalendars. Refreshing relies on the optional onSuccess prop. CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88 passes onChanged, which invalidates connectedCalendars, but EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-376 renders SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper without onChanged, so onSuccess is undefined there. After deleting the cache in that view, the dropdown keeps showing the old cacheUpdatedAt and the delete option until a reload.
